title: When the Songbook Breaks Again
premise: Ansel Sterling, a wedding planner whose own engagement ended in a scandal she's never explained, is forced to chaperone a corporate pen-pal program that accidentally pairs her bitter rival, Theo Vance, with an anonymous writer — Ansel herself. As their letters deepen, Ansel must decide whether to confess the decade-old betrayal that destroyed both their careers, knowing Theo is about to accept a job that will take him abroad forever. In the end, she reads her final letter aloud at the wedding she's coordinating, says the rehearsed sentence — 'It was me, and I'm sorry' — and chooses truth over survival, winning a second chance she never believed she deserved.
about_author: H. M. Ravensworth is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent ten years watching other people's love stories from behind the cake table. Ravensworth writes romances about people who arrive too late, say too little, and finally learn to say the sentence that matters.

chapters.title: The Planner Who Doesn't Believe
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She orchestrates a flawless wedding for a couple she envies, then returns to her empty office where a corporate memo announces a mandatory pen-pal morale program she must administer. The beat is weary competence masking grief; she catalogs other people's happiness like inventory she can never purchase.

chapters.title: Mismatched by Machine
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A software glitch pairs pen pals at random — and pairs her rival Theo Vance, now a consultant hired to audit her failing company, with the anonymous handle she uses to test the system. Their first exchange is acid and wit; neither knows the other's face. The beat is reluctant spark.

chapters.title: Letters in the Margins
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. By day, Ansel and Theo spar in conference rooms over budget cuts; by night, their letters turn startlingly honest. Theo confesses a career ruined ten years ago by someone he trusted. Ansel recognizes the story — because she caused it. The beat is dread blooming inside intimacy.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Flashback to the betrayal: a decade ago, Ansel took credit for Theo's design and let him take the fall, trading truth for survival. Now she drafts a confession letter a dozen times and deletes it each time. The beat is the weight of an unsaid sentence grown too heavy to lift.

chapters.title: Two Tables at One Wedding
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo is hired to plan the company's anniversary gala — Ansel's biggest event — and begins noticing the anonymous pen pal's phrases surfacing in Ansel's speech. Suspicion and attraction tangle. The beat is the thrill of almost-knowing, and the fear of what knowing will cost.

chapters.title: What Survival Bought
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Theo announces he's accepted a position abroad, departing in three weeks — right after the gala. Ansel realizes her window to confess is closing. She sabotages her own chance, sending a letter that pushes him away to make the goodbye easier. The beat is self-protective cowardice curdling into regret.

chapters.title: The Unsent Draft
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Hurt by the cold letter, Theo digs into the pen-pal system's logs, chasing the anonymous handle. He finds the routing error and the sender's terminal ID: Ansel's office. He says nothing, testing her instead with a letter quoting her oldest secret. The beat is quiet, devastating certainty.

chapters.title: Gala Eve
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The night before the gala, Theo confronts her with the evidence — not with fury, but with a question: 'Why didn't you ever say it?' Ansel's rehearsed sentence fails her; she can only apologize for the apology being late. He leaves. The beat is collapse — identity and loyalty both forfeit.

chapters.title: When the Songbook Breaks
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The gala: Ansel abandons her script mid-toast, takes the microphone, and reads her final letter aloud — the confession, the sentence, ten years late — in front of everyone, choosing truth over the career survival demands she protect. The beat is public ruin offered as a gift.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Weeks later: Ansel, unemployed but unburdened, finds Theo waiting at the airport he never boarded from — he'd deferred the job. They begin as pen pals again, faces known this time, writing the first honest letters of their lives. The beat is tender, earned hope: love arriving exactly when the truth finally did.
